decisions.reason: Although it is close to our existing infrared-heating know-how, the low-noise burner showed only minimal market visibility after launch, so we would fold any useful learning back into the core range rather than keep a weak standalone offer.

The gas infrared plaque heater fits our established technical base and customer applications, and its dedicated product page suggests enough early commercial relevance to justify continued refinement and market support.

While related to our core capabilities, the gas infrared luminous radiant heater showed limited visible traction, so under a focused portfolio strategy we would reallocate resources to stronger adjacent products.
This tube-heater launch is technically close to what we already know, but with only a brief mention and no stronger later signal, it looks like an incremental variant not worth separate continuation.

The standard gas infrared plaque heater is strongly aligned with our existing knowledge base and customer needs, and its own product page indicates a sufficiently solid market position to keep developing it.

Given the narrow portfolio, the duplicate tube-heater positioning, and weak standalone market evidence, we would discontinue this variant and concentrate learning and development on more clearly established lines.
